strategies.summary: At init time, fold each BatchNorm's scale/bias/mean/var/eps into the preceding Conv2d weight and bias tensors, eliminating all BN kernel launches at inference. Every Conv+BN pair becomes a single conv with absorbed affine parameters. This removes27 separate BN kernel dispatches across the 14 conv_bn/conv_dw blocks.
implementation_hints: After building self.model, iterate all Sequential blocks and locate Conv2d immediately followed by BatchNorm2d; absorb BN running_mean, running_var, weight, bias, and eps into new Conv2d weight and bias using the standard w' = gamma*w/sqrt(var+eps), b' = beta - gamma*mean/sqrt(var+eps) formulas
Replace the nn.BatchNorm2d module in each Sequential with nn.Identity() after folding so the graph structure stays intact
For depthwise conv (groups=inp), fold per-channel BN params channel-wise along dim=0 of the weight tensor
Call model.eval() before folding to ensure running stats are the inference values; store folded weights as nn.Parameter with requires_grad=False
No changes needed in forward_stmt_2 â the model.forward() call already handles the updated graph
strategies.expected_gain: Removes ~27 BN kernel launches (memory-bandwidth-bound round trips to global memory per forward pass); estimated15â30% latency reduction on smaller spatial resolutions where BN dominates
risk_notes: Must run in eval mode; folded weights are incorrect in training mode
Preserve epsilon from each BN's eps attribute â do not hardcode
Depthwise conv weight shape is (inp, 1, 3, 3); fold along dim=0 only
Do not change output dtype or shape
forbidden_patterns: changing forward signature
hardcoding eps
running folding on non-eval model

review_notes.openai-compatible: Strongest risk-adjusted option for inference: folding BN into preceding conv is standard, removes BN launches entirely, preserves outputs when using running stats and per-layer eps, and requires no fragile custom kernel work. Very likely useful if eval-only.
review_notes.claude-compatible: BN folding into Conv2d weights is the highest-value, lowest-risk strategy here. It is mathematically exact in eval mode, requires no custom CUDA, eliminates all BN kernel launches in one pass, and the depthwise weight folding along dim=0 is straightforward. The only real risk is ensuring eval mode is set before folding and preserving per-layer eps. Strongly recommended as the first thing to try.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Folding BatchNorm into Convolution weights is a highly effective and classic optimization that eliminates BN overhead entirely. However, it is only valid in evaluation mode and will fail if the benchmark requires training/gradient checks.

strategies.summary: Convert the input tensor and all model parameters to channels_last (NHWC) memory format at the start of forward. cuDNN selects substantially more efficient NHWC-native kernels for both3x3 depthwise convolutions and 1x1 pointwise convolutions when channel counts are multiples of 8 (32/64/128/256/512/1024 all qualify), bypassing the generic indexed accessor kernel observed in the NCU profile.

In forward_stmt_1, add x = x.to(memory_format=torch.channels_last) as the first line to convert the input once per forward call
The NHWC-optimized cuDNN depthwise kernel avoids the generic GenericPackedTensorAccessor path that limits occupancy to 1 warp; it uses vectorized 128-bit loads and higher register efficiency
All channels in MobileNetV1 with alpha=1.0 are multiples of 32, satisfying cuDNN's vectorization alignment requirements
No custom CUDA code needed; the gain comes entirely from cuDNN kernel selection
strategies.expected_gain: cuDNN NHWC depthwise kernels typically achieve 2â4x higher occupancy versus the generic NCHW path; combined with vectorized memory access, expect 25â50% end-to-end speedup on the depthwise-dominated layers
risk_notes: Output tensor will also be channels_last; final view() in forward_stmt_3 will still work correctly as view() sees a contiguous logical shape
If the benchmark harness compares output to a reference that is contiguous NCHW, add .contiguous() before return if needed
Do not change I/O shape or dtype
forbidden_patterns: mixing NCHW and NHWC tensors within a single conv layer
calling contiguous() inside the hot path unnecessarily

review_notes.openai-compatible: High-value low-risk strategy. Switching model/input to `channels_last` often materially improves cuDNN depthwise and pointwise conv kernel selection on MobileNet-like shapes, with minimal code change and preserved semantics. One of the best practical bets here.
review_notes.claude-compatible: Channels-last (NHWC) conversion is a high-leverage, zero-custom-CUDA change. All MobileNetV1 channel counts are multiples of 32 which satisfies cuDNN alignment requirements. The 2-4x occupancy improvement claim for depthwise kernels is well-supported in practice. The only real risk is ensuring the output is contiguous if the harness compares byte-for-byte, which is a one-liner to fix. Strong candidate to combine with strategy_02.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Converting the model and inputs to channels_last (NHWC) memory format is a low-risk, high-reward strategy. cuDNN has highly optimized NHWC kernels for depthwise convolutions that significantly outperform NCHW, and this preserves full autograd support.

"""
        MobileNetV1 architecture implementation.

        :param num_classes: The number of output classes (default: 1000)
        :param input_channels: The number of input channels (default: 3 for RGB images)
        :param alpha: Width multiplier (default: 1.0)
        """
def conv_bn(inp, oup, stride):
            return nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(inp, oup, 3, stride, 1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(oup),
                nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
            )
def conv_dw(inp, oup, stride):
            return nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(inp, inp, 3, stride, 1, groups=inp, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(inp),
                nn.ReLU(inplace=True),

                nn.Conv2d(inp, oup, 1, 1, 0, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(oup),
                nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            )
self.model = nn.Sequential(
            conv_bn(input_channels, int(32 * alpha), 2),
            conv_dw(int(32 * alpha), int(64 * alpha), 1),
            conv_dw(int(64 * alpha), int(128 * alpha), 2),
            conv_dw(int(128 * alpha), int(128 * alpha), 1),
            conv_dw(int(128 * alpha), int(256 * alpha), 2),
            conv_dw(int(256 * alpha), int(256 * alpha), 1),
            conv_dw(int(256 * alpha), int(512 * alpha), 2),
            conv_dw(int(512 * alpha), int(512 * alpha), 1),
            conv_dw(int(512 * alpha), int(512 * alpha), 1),
            conv_dw(int(512 * alpha), int(512 * alpha), 1),
            conv_dw(int(512 * alpha), int(512 * alpha), 1),
            conv_dw(int(512 * alpha), int(512 * alpha), 1),
            conv_dw(int(512 * alpha), int(1024 * alpha), 2),
            conv_dw(int(1024 * alpha), int(1024 * alpha), 1),
            nn.AvgPool2d(7),
        )
self.fc = nn.Linear(int(1024 * alpha), num_classes)
